documents.unit: Center for the Advancement of Teaching
documents.title: Sample Syllabus Statements for the Use of AI Tools in Your Course
tiers: Acceptable and Unacceptable Use of AI
documents.summary: The teaching center gives three sample syllabus statements that instructors can adapt: limited use with permitted and barred activities, encouraged use, and full prohibition. Each ties AI use to academic honesty and leaves penalties for the instructor to fill in.
documents.stance_why: The document offers three templates and says "Please adjust the guidance to fit your particular context", so it sets no single stance and hands the choice to instructors; the tiers are limited, encouraged and prohibited.

units.why: The template is offered so instructors can build their own course policy; "Please adjust the guidance to fit your particular context" hands the decision to each instructor, so this is per-instructor setting (P04) rather than a university rule.
units.anchor: Please adjust the guidance to fit your particular context.

units.why: The sample statements are three named options (limited use, encouraged use, prohibited), which is a set of tiers; "Acceptable and Unacceptable Use of AI" is the limited tier. P05 fits better than P04 because the point is the named categories.
units.anchor: Acceptable and Unacceptable Use of AI
units.frag_start: Acceptable and Unacceptable Use of AI
units.frag_end: Acceptable and Unacceptable Use of AI
units.policy: The guidance offers three sample syllabus statements: acceptable and unacceptable use of AI, use encouraged and permitted, and use prohibited.
units.resolution_why: Coder A anchored the 'certain purposes, but not for others' sentence and coder B the 'Acceptable and Unacceptable Use of AI' heading; both are P05 for the same passage (the sample statements are named tiers). Kept coder B's anchor and normalized policy.

units.why: "Remember also to note in specific assignment descriptions where AI use is allowed or disallowed" tells instructors to state expectations at assignment level too, an instruction to communicate rules (P09), not a stance.
units.anchor: note in specific assignment descriptions where AI use is allowed or disallowed
units.policy: Instructors note in specific assignment descriptions where AI use is allowed or disallowed.

units.why: "Brainstorming and refining your ideas" is listed under the activities for which generative AI "is permitted in this course", so it allows AI for brainstorming (P15).
units.anchor: Brainstorming and refining your ideas;

units.why: "Fine tuning your research questions" is a permitted exploratory use; P15 (exploring approaches) is the nearest type.
units.anchor: Fine tuning your research questions;

units.why: "Finding information on your topic" is permitted; AI is used like a search tool to learn about a topic, matching P12 (tutor or search engine for understanding).
units.anchor: Finding information on your topic;

units.why: "Drafting an outline to organize your thoughts" is a permitted use; it is writing support, not code, so P91 fits the permission itself.
units.anchor: Drafting an outline to organize your thoughts;

units.why: "Checking grammar and style" is listed as permitted; it is proofreading support, which is P91.
units.anchor: Checking grammar and style.

units.why: The not-permitted list bars "Impersonating you in classroom contexts", with examples of discussion board prompts or Zoom chat; this is AI substituting for the student in course communication, near P58.
units.anchor: Impersonating you in classroom contexts
units.policy: Generative AI use is not permitted for impersonating you in classroom contexts, such as composing discussion board prompts assigned to you or content you put into a Zoom chat.
units.fit_note: Covers discussion board posts and Zoom chat among classmates, not only messages to course staff.

units.why: "Completing group work that your group has assigned to you, unless it is mutually agreed" bars AI from doing a student's assigned part of group work, closest to P19.
units.anchor: Completing group work that your group has assigned to you
units.policy: Generative AI use is not permitted for completing group work that your group has assigned to you, unless it is mutually agreed upon that you may utilize the tool.
units.fit_note: The exception depends on mutual agreement of the group, which the type does not capture. Coder A coded this UNCOVERED: AI may not do one's assigned share of group work unless the group mutually agrees to its use.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: UNCOVERED (group-agreed AI use); coder B: P19. The source lists it under what AI is 'not permitted' for: 'Completing group work that your group has assigned to you', i.e. AI doing the student's assigned work. That is the P19 rule, with a group-consensus exception that the fit_note records, so P19 follows rather than a new type.

units.why: "Writing a draft of a writing assignment" is in the not-permitted list; AI may not produce the draft a student submits, which is P19.
units.anchor: Writing a draft of a writing assignment.

units.why: "Writing entire sentences, paragraphs or papers to complete class assignments" bars AI from producing text submitted for assignments, which is P19.
units.anchor: Writing entire sentences, paragraphs or papers to complete class assignments.

units.why: "You are responsible for the information you submit based on an AI query" places responsibility for submitted work on the student, fitting P29.
units.anchor: You are responsible for the information you submit based on an AI query
units.policy: Students are responsible for the information they submit based on an AI query, for instance that it does not violate intellectual property laws or contain misinformation or unethical content.
units.fit_note: Names IP, misinformation and unethical content as the specific things the student answers for.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B split the parenthetical into separate P31 (misinformation) and P52 (intellectual property) units, and re-coded the repeat of the responsibility sentence in the encouraged tier. Coder A coded one P29 unit. The source gives IP laws, misinformation and unethical content as examples ('for instance') of what the student is responsible for, so they are one rule, not distinct duties; the repeat in the encouraged tier is an exact repeat within the document. I kept the single P29 unit and dropped the three extra units.

units.why: "must be properly documented and cited in order to stay within university policies on academic honesty" requires citing any AI use in the limited tier, which is P24.
units.anchor: must be properly documented and cited in order to stay within university policies
units.policy: Use of AI tools must be properly documented and cited in order to stay within university policies on academic honesty.

units.why: The template tells instructors to "[Insert citation style for your discipline", so instructors choose how AI is cited; closest to P25 but it names no required elements such as tool or prompt.
units.anchor: Insert citation style for your discipline.
units.policy: Instructors insert the citation style for their discipline.
units.fit_note: Leaves the citation format to the instructor and names no required details such as prompt or output.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded this. The template tells instructors to insert a citation style for their discipline, a real instruction about how AI use is cited. It is not a full P25 rule (no tool, prompt or output required), so I kept P25 with the fit_note.

units.why: "Any assignment that is found to have used generative AI tools in unauthorized ways [insert the penalty here*]" says unauthorized use carries a penalty the instructor writes in, so penalties are stated in advance (P37).
units.anchor: Any assignment that is found to have used generative AI tools in unauthorized ways
units.policy: Any assignment found to have used generative AI tools in unauthorized ways receives a penalty the instructor states in the syllabus.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: actor instructor, phase course-start, modality should (the instructor is told to insert a penalty). Coder B: actor student, phase when-misuse, modality informs. The sentence is syllabus text that tells students a penalty follows unauthorized AI use, with a slot for the instructor to fill in. It binds the student and concerns the consequence of misuse, so student, when-misuse, informs.

units.why: "When in doubt about permitted usage, please ask for clarification" tells students to ask when unsure, which is P10.
units.anchor: When in doubt about permitted usage, please ask for clarification.

units.why: "You are welcome/expected to use generative AI tools" in the encouraged tier welcomes or expects AI use, which is P02.
units.anchor: You are welcome/expected to use generative AI tools
units.frag_end: learning goal use of AI aligns with].
units.policy: Students are welcome or expected to use generative AI tools in the class because doing so aligns with the course learning goal.
units.fit_note: Template leaves it to the instructor to choose between welcome and expected.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: phase general, modality may; coder B: phase during-work, modality should. The sentence sets the course's default stance on AI ('welcome/expected to use ... in this class'), not a rule about a particular piece of work, so phase is general. 'Welcome/expected' leans to encouragement, so modality should, matching P02 and the encourage unit stance.

units.why: "aligns with the course learning goal [insert the course learning goal use of AI aligns with]" ties permission for AI to a stated learning goal, so P83.
units.anchor: doing so aligns with the course learning goal
units.policy: Instructors tie encouraged AI use to a stated course learning goal.

units.why: The prohibited template says generative AI tools "are not permitted in this class", a total ban for any purpose, which is P01.
units.anchor: are not permitted in this class
units.frag_start: The use of generative AI tools (such
units.policy: Generative AI tools are not permitted in this class.

units.why: "any use of AI tools for work in this class may be considered a violation of Temple University's Academic Honesty policy and Student Conduct Code" classifies use as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: may be considered a violation of Temple University’s Academic Honesty policy and Student Conduct Code
units.frag_end: since the work is not your own.
units.policy: Any use of AI tools for work in the class may be considered a violation of Temple University's Academic Honesty policy and Student Conduct Code, since the work is not your own.

units.why: "since the work is not your own" gives the reason for the ban, that AI output is not the student's own work, matching P29.
units.anchor: since the work is not your own.
units.frag_end: since the work is not your own.
units.fit_note: Used as the stated reason for a ban, not as a duty.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded this. 'since the work is not your own' is the stated reason for the total ban, a rationale statement, which the codebook counts as a policy unit (modality informs). Kept as P29 with the fit_note.

units.why: "The use of unauthorized AI tools will result in [insert the penalty here*]" says a penalty follows unauthorized use, with the instructor setting it; P37.
units.anchor: The use of unauthorized AI tools will result in [insert the penalty here*]
units.policy: The use of unauthorized AI tools will result in a penalty the instructor states in the syllabus.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: actor instructor, phase course-start, modality should (the instructor is told to insert a penalty). Coder B: actor student, phase when-misuse, modality informs. The sentence is syllabus text that tells students a penalty follows unauthorized AI use, with a slot for the instructor to fill in. It binds the student and concerns the consequence of misuse, so student, when-misuse, informs.

units.why: "have conversations in your department about the appropriate penalties" asks departments to agree on penalties together; P37 is about stating penalties, not deciding them jointly, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: have conversations in your department about the appropriate penalties
units.policy: Departments should discuss and agree on appropriate penalties for unauthorized AI use.
units.uncovered_note: Instructors are advised to agree on penalties for unauthorized AI use together within their department.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded this as its own unit (coder A merged it with the next sentence under P37 with a fit_note). 'We highly recommend that you have conversations in your department about the appropriate penalties' is a distinct recommendation to agree on penalties jointly, which P37 (state penalties in advance) does not cover, so it is kept as UNCOVERED.

units.why: "appropriate level of penalty for first-time offenders and those who repeatedly violate" says penalties should differ by offense count, matching "escalation by offense" in P37.
units.anchor: appropriate level of penalty for first-time offenders and those who repeatedly violate
units.frag_end: policies on the use of AI.
units.policy: Instructors think about the appropriate level of penalty for first-time offenders and for those who repeatedly violate their AI policies.
units.fit_note: Recommends thinking about penalty levels by offense count rather than stating a penalty. Coder A's fit_note on the same passage: recommends departmental discussion of penalty levels rather than stating penalties.

documents.title: Generative AI and Chatbots (research guide)
documents.summary: A library research guide on generative AI chatbots, mostly tool advice. One paragraph states the university rule: AI is prohibited in a class unless the instructor grants permission, and unauthorized use is academic misconduct.
documents.stance_why: Coder A: restrict; coder B: delegates. The guide states the university rule, 'Temple policy prohibits the use of generative AI tools in a class, unless the instructor explicitly grants permission', a default ban with explicit permission as the exception, which is the definition of restrict. It also says 'Different instructors may have different rules', but that explains where the exceptions come from and does not remove the default. So restrict.

units.why: "Temple policy prohibits the use of generative AI tools in a class, unless the instructor explicitly grants permission" sets a default ban with instructor-granted exceptions, which is P01.
units.anchor: prohibits the use of generative AI tools in a class, unless the instructor explicitly
units.policy: Temple policy prohibits the use of generative AI tools in a class, unless the instructor explicitly grants permission.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: one unit typed P06 (fallback when syllabus silent); coder B: two units for the same sentence, P01 and P06. The sentence 'Temple policy prohibits the use of generative AI tools in a class, unless the instructor explicitly grants permission' states one rule, a default ban with instructor-granted exceptions, which is P01. It does not say what applies when a syllabus is silent, so P06 would restate the same rule. I kept one P01 unit and dropped the duplicate P06 unit.

units.why: "Student Code of Conduct defines unauthorized use of generative AI as academic misconduct" classifies unauthorized AI use as misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: defines unauthorized use of generative AI as academic misconduct
units.policy: Temple's Student Code of Conduct defines unauthorized use of generative AI as academic misconduct.

units.why: "Different instructors may have different rules" says the rule varies by instructor, fitting P04.
units.anchor: Different instructors may have different rules related to the use of generative AI.

units.why: "Students should read their syllabi carefully to learn what is permitted in a class" makes students responsible for learning each course's rules (P78).
units.anchor: Students should read their syllabi carefully to learn what is permitted in a class.

units.why: "We encourage you to test out AI tools and chatbots, rather than simply reading about them!" welcomes experimenting with AI (P02), with no rule attached.
units.anchor: We encourage you to test out AI tools and chatbots
units.fit_note: Library encouragement to experiment, not a course-level default rule.

units.why: "Temple Libraries is here to support your use of generative AI chatbots" states the guide's purpose and scope, an institution-level framing statement (P56).
units.anchor: Temple Libraries is here to support your use of generative AI chatbots
units.fit_note: A library guide's statement of support and purpose, not an institution-wide framework.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded this. 'Temple Libraries is here to support your use of generative AI chatbots' states the guide's purpose and stance of support, a rationale-type statement, so it is kept as informs with a fit_note because P56 is about institution-wide frameworks.

units.why: The self-paced tutorial teaches how chatbots work, their strengths and weaknesses, and how they "may help or hinder learning", an AI-literacy offering for students (P70).
units.anchor: Upon completion of this self-paced tutorial
units.policy: The libraries offer a self-paced tutorial on how chatbots work, their strengths and weaknesses, and how they may help or hinder learning.

units.why: "Make an appointment with a subject librarian or specialist" directs users to human help alongside AI tools (P72).
units.anchor: Make an appointment
units.resolution_why: Coder A: modality may; coder B: informs. The guide invites users to make an appointment with a librarian, which is an offer rather than a fact, so may.

units.why: "Request a past workshop recording" offers recordings of library workshops on generative AI, a training resource (P70).
units.anchor: Request a past workshop recording
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded this. The guide offers recordings of past library workshops on generative AI, a training resource for students, which fits P70. Kept.

notes: Reconciled from coder A and coder B. The saved PDF text has one word per line; anchors are exact after whitespace folding. Tier templates repeat the responsibility and citation sentences; repeats are coded once. Guide page text is thin; navigation menu items were not coded. Document-level stance for temple-u2 resolved to restrict (coder B had delegates).
